title: Regional contingency runbook: GPU continuity and warm-standby corridors (Q4 2025)
body:
Purpose and summary:
This doc defines a contingency-oriented, region-aware runbook for GPU continuity across Redwood production regions. It focuses on warm-standby corridors (short-term burst capacity routed between region pairs), prefilling strategies, and an operational checklist to ensure we can survive a region-level capacity loss without customer-visible throttling or large latency regressions.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API and Dedicated serving pools (does not change Private network procedures).
- Covers N+1 local capacity strategies, cross-region warm-standby corridors, and emergency burst policies for first 24 hours after detection.
- Not a financial approval doc; contains cost estimates for contingency scenarios.

Key definitions (short):
- Warm-standby corridor: a pre-provisioned, low-utilization GPU pool in a sibling region configured to accept redirected traffic within 5-10 minutes with minimal cold-start cost.
- Evacuation window: the target time from detection to traffic fully routed to fallback (goal = 30 minutes).
- Reserve margin: fraction of total peak capacity earmarked as spare across regions for DR (standard target = 12%).

Assumptions (baseline):
- Global 95th percentile token throughput at current baseline (Oct 2025): 1.85M tokens/min.
- Average per-GPU throughput for primary models: 14.5k tokens/min (mixed fp16/8 performance profile).
- Typical per-region peak share: us-west-1 36%, us-east-1 28%, eu-west-1 22%, ap-east-1 14% (subject to change).
- Target customer-impact threshold: <2% request throttling + <15% latency increase for top 90% of routes during first 24h.

Design targets (what we want):
- Maintain 12% global reserve margin during business-as-usual, distributed such that no region holds <8% and no region >18% of reserves by percentage of regional peak.
- Two warm-standby corridors: us-west-1 <-> us-east-1 and eu-west-1 <-> ap-east-1. Corridors chosen for latency/cost tradeoffs and available cross-region bandwidth.
- Evacuation window: full traffic cutover within 30 minutes, graceful ramping over 10 minutes with circuit-breaker monitoring.

Regional capacity snapshot (text table, current allocations and proposed warm pools):
Region | Baseline GPUs | Peak GPUs needed | Current spare | Proposed warm corridor pool
us-west-1 | 520 | 620 | 60 (11.5%) | 40 GPUs (to be reserved in us-east-1 corridor)
us-east-1 | 410 | 470 | 48 (11.7%) | 36 GPUs (warm for us-west-1 overflow)
eu-west-1 | 310 | 360 | 34 (11.0%) | 28 GPUs (warm for ap-east-1 overflow)
ap-east-1 | 180 | 220 | 20 (11.1%) | 18 GPUs (warm for eu-west-1 overflow)
Notes: baseline numbers rounded to nearest 10. Warm corridor pools are logical reservations (either hot nodes spun but idled at low utilization or pre-approved capacity in cloud provider contracts flagged for our use).

Activation triggers (automated + manual):
1) Automated: region-level monitored metric breach (sustained 90th-percentile GPU saturations >92% for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows) triggers preflight.
2) Manual: SRE/Infra oncall can declare "region compromised" if network isolation, provider outage, or Scheduled maintenance >2 hours.
3) Safety net: downstream product teams can request fast-failover if customer-impacting anomalies detected.

Failover phases (sequence):
- Preflight (0-5 minutes): lock configuration, snapshot KV cache metadata, mark canary routes for limited traffic to verify warm pools. Run autoscaler override to prevent scale-down of warm nodes.
- Canary verification (5-15 minutes): route 1-3% of selected low-latency routes to warm corridor; validate model correctness and latency regression <20% for canaries.
- Ramp (15-30 minutes): gradually move remaining traffic in 5% increments, monitor token-level latency, cost, and error spikes. Engage circuit-breakers if error rate >5x baseline for >2 min.
- Stabilize (30-240 minutes): autoscale to steady-state and re-balance KV cache priming if persistent >6 hours.

Prefill / KV cache strategy:
- Critical models: pre-warm KV caches for top 50 prompt prefixes using lightweight synthetic requests prior to routing bulk traffic. Maintain prefilling keys in S3/Metadata store so warm pools can prime within 10 minutes.
- For long-running sessions (chat), allow session handoff only if KV checkpoint exists; otherwise use partial warm routing and degrade to stateless fallback after 20 minutes.

Routing and policy configuration (ops playbook snippets):
- Smart routing policy: in failover, route by route-weighting first to warm corridor with bin-packing by token-size and latency-sensitivity metadata.
- Cost banding: prioritize high-SLA customers to lowest-latency fallback (dedicated reserved nodes in sibling region) while best-effort customers routed to lower-cost reserved pooled quantized models.
- Rate limiting: reduce burst window from 20s to 8s for non-SLA tenants during initial 60 minutes to avoid cascading autoscaling.

Operational runbook checklist (first 6 items to act on):
1) Pager triage: confirm outage region and impact vector.
2) Lock autoscaler policies in affected region to avoid noisy scale events.
3) Enable warm corridor (flip pre-allocated gateway routes).
4) Start canary traffic and validate model outputs against baseline checksums.
5) Monitor 1-minute token latency and 1-minute error rates in dedicated dashboard.
6) Run cost-override to allow emergency burst beyond typical budget for up to 12 hours (notify finance later).

Cost and financial note (rough):
- Keeping the warm corridor idle but available (hot idled GPUs + reserved IPs) costs ~0.9x of full active cost per GPU due to idling charge on cloud provider contracts and snapshot storage. For proposed pools above, monthly contingency cost estimate = $170k (one-time Q4 estimate; depends on negotiated reserved instance discounts).

Testing and drills:
- Quarterly tabletop: run a simulated us-west-1 capacity loss drill targeting evacuation window 30 min. Document latency and customer impact.
- Biannual full drill: conduct live 2-hour failover test for low-risk routes to exercise cache prefill and routing automation.

Telemetry and SLO updates:
- New dashboard: "Corridor Health" with metrics: corridor-available, canary-latency, cache-prefill-status, route-weight.
- Update SLOs for 24h DR window: customers on Hosted API will have a DR latency allowance of +10% for non-SLA routes and up to +25% for SLA routes before crediting.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Approve long-term warm corridor billing model: hot-idle vs burst-on-demand with fast provisioning (cost vs readiness).
- Decide ownership of corridor-prefill metadata (apply to platform or product teams).
- Confirm final percentage target for global reserve margin (12% proposed, CFO may request 8% vs Ops preference for 15%).

Action items (next 30 days):
- Ramp: Infra to provision IaC templates for corridor pools (PR #214 referenced). Owner: Ethan. Due: 2025-11-07.
- Finance: provide contingency budget approval for Q4 warm corridors. Owner: Aisha. Due: 2025-11-14.
- SRE: build corridor health dashboard and automated trigger rules. Owner: Liam. Due: 2025-11-21.

References and appendices:
- Ticket with baseline telemetry: JIRA INFRA-4821 (gpu-throttle-alerts).
- GPU capacity catalog: Confluence /display/INF/GPU+Capacity+Catalog.
- Related infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/214

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an operational draft; numbers are conservative and intended to be re-calibrated after the first drill. Please comment in-line with additional region candidates or objections to corridor pairings.
